head_commit.message:
fix(fbx): BlenderRunner.run() never populated output_hash, so every real conversion reported status=failed

Audit finding (lane-link/FBX cooking-readiness verification, 2026-09-24): the
real, non-mocked BlenderRunner.run() declared BlenderResult.output_hash but
never assigned it after producing the FBX (input_hash was correctly set from
self._hash_file(self.obj_path), but the analogous self._hash_file(fbx_path)
call for output_hash was missing). Since output_hash defaulted to "",
`output_hash_ok = bool(result.output_hash) and ...` was always False, so
`checks_ok = all([...])` was always False and every real conversion reported
status="failed" -- even when Blender genuinely succeeded and produced a valid
FBX. This directly breaks tile_fbx_generator.generate_tile_fbx()'s real
production path (the exact code the CARLA Large-Map tile cook will call).

The bug was invisible to the existing test suite because every test in
test_blender_conversion_integrity.py uses FakeBlenderRunner, which overrides
run() entirely and already set result.output_hash itself in its own
reimplementation -- so the real BlenderRunner.run() path was never exercised.

Verified live against the real Blender 4.3 binary and a real OSM2World-
produced OBJ (61 objects) from this repo's production-readiness artifacts:
RED (pre-fix) -> status=failed, failed_checks=['output_hash_match'];
GREEN (post-fix) -> status=ok, output_hash_match=true, and a follow-up
run_fbx_roundtrip() gave ROUNDTRIP_PASS (61/61 objects match, 0 diffs).

Added test_t_real_runner_sets_output_hash_and_reports_ok, which exercises the
real BlenderRunner (not the fake) with only subprocess.run mocked, and
confirmed it fails without the fix and passes with it.

Full bare pytest suite: 6189 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed.

head_commit.message:
fix(gap024): atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL acquire + stale-owner clobber guard in WriterLock

WriterLock.acquire() was a plain check-then-write (TOCTOU): exists()/is_live()
check, then an unconditional plain-text write, with nothing atomic gating who
actually wins. Reproduced with 8 real multiprocessing.Process workers (spawn
context) racing a fresh lock across 20 iterations: 20/20 had all 8 workers
succeed simultaneously.

Switched acquire() to a genuine atomic create-exclusive primitive:
os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY) is the sole arbiter of "who wins";
reclaiming an expired/malformed lock unlinks it and retries the same
O_EXCL create rather than writing unconditionally, so a concurrent
reclaimer racing the same unlink is harmless -- only the next O_EXCL call
decides ownership.

Also fixed a related bug: a stale (expired-lease) owner's own in-memory
WriterLock object could call .heartbeat() or .release() and silently
overwrite a DIFFERENT agent's legitimately-reclaimed lock, because neither
method re-validated the currently-persisted lock's identity before writing.
Both now re-read the on-disk lock and refuse (raise RuntimeError) if its
lock_id no longer matches this handle's, rather than trusting only their
own remembered state.

WriterLock.save() (which now backs heartbeat()/release()'s actual writes)
was also upgraded to the mkstemp+fsync+os.replace pattern already used by
Manifest.save() in ultimate_pipeline/artifacts/model.py, for the same
"atomically replace this file's contents" reason that pattern exists there.

New committed regression tests (tests/unit/test_writer_lock_concurrency.py):
- real multi-process TOCTOU race (8 workers x 20 iterations, exactly one
  winner required each time)
- stale-owner heartbeat/release clobber, now asserted to raise
- 5 corrupt/unknown-schema-at-acquire cases (invalid JSON, JSON list,
  unrecognized extra key, unknown schema string with valid fields, empty
  file) re-verified to still fail closed under the new implementation

head_commit.message:
fix(gap021): pin Osm2Odr proj_string explicitly instead of relying on CARLA's default

ultimate_pipeline/osm/osm_to_xodr_wrapper.py built a carla.Osm2OdrSettings
object and called carla.Osm2Odr.convert() with it but never assigned
settings.proj_string anywhere, so every conversion silently inherited
whatever the installed CARLA build's own Osm2OdrSettings() defaults to
(reproduced: literal bare "+proj=tmerc", no datum/units) instead of an
explicit, version-independent value.

Investigation (not just the originally-suspected fix) found that "fixing"
this by pointing proj_string at *true* EPSG:32632
(+lon_0=9 +k=0.9996 +x_0=500000) would have been an active regression:
a real conversion of a small real-coordinate Ingolstadt-area OSM fixture
through carla.Osm2Odr.convert() on this machine's CARLA 0.9.16 confirmed
that proj_string genuinely controls the output geometry's numeric
coordinates (not header-only), and switching it to true EPSG:32632 shifts
the produced geometry by >150 km relative to the frame the rest of this
codebase already depends on. That frame -- Osm2Odr's native bare tmerc(0,0)
-- is the SAME one already established and verified across
dem_crs_contract.py (F1 CRS contract / OSM2ODR_NATIVE_PROJ4),
coordinate_control.py (VERIFIED_XODR_GEOMETRY_CRS_PROJ4), and
osm_polygon_loader.py (PROJ_STRING), and is what the frozen
auto_map_of_record candidate's local-rebase frame is itself derived from
(carla_tools/map_registry.py).

Fix: explicitly set proj_string to the literal
ultimate_pipeline.enrichment.osm_polygon_loader.PROJ_STRING value (so the
pre-existing "georef_proj_consistency" textual-equality check in
stage_04_enrichment.py / main_pipeline.py now genuinely passes instead of
comparing two differently-spelled-but-equivalent tmerc strings), and set
use_offsets=False alongside the existing center_map=False (CARLA's own
use_offsets default is True, which combined with center_map=False
triggers Osm2Odr's "Could not write OpenDRIVE geoReference" warning).

Verified via a real, non-mocked conversion: the produced XODR's header
<geoReference>, inverse-projected, resolves the fixture's real-world
coordinate to within 0.005 m (round-trip), and the header text now
literally equals OSMPolygonLoader.PROJ_STRING.

Added tests/unit/test_osm_to_xodr_proj_string_gap021.py: asserts the
config's proj_string is pinned to the correct literal/numeric frame (and
explicitly not to true EPSG:32632), and end-to-end converts a small
real-coordinate fixture and checks the produced header round-trips to the
real-world location.

fix(domain-gap-gnn): source-SHA exclusion contract, closes GAP-010

Root cause: build_training_dataset_manifest() globbed ALL *.xodr in
tiles_dir with zero source-identity exclusion -- any file present,
including a duplicate of a held-out eval map, silently became training
data. MapTileDataset had only filename-based exclude_names, nothing
content-hash-based.

Fix, wired into both the trainer and K-sweep paths (not just one):
- gnn_provenance.py: new exclusion_hashes_for() helper;
  build_training_dataset_manifest() gains exclude_source_hashes=
  (backward-compatible, default None).
- map_tile_dataset.py: MapTileDataset gains exclude_source_hashes=,
  recorded as EXCLUDED_BY_POLICY/source_sha_excluded.
- train_map_encoder.py: new --exclude_source_xodr CLI arg.
- run_ksweep.py: the run's own eval pair (manual_xodr/auto_xodr) is now
  ALWAYS excluded automatically; --exclude_source_xodr adds more;
  _list_tiles() filters by hash BEFORE nested_subsets() selection;
  exclusion set forwarded to the trainer subprocess and recorded in
  ksweep_report.json.

Verified end-to-end on real data, not synthetic: injected a literal copy
of the real eval file into a real union_tiles subset -> pre-fix
audit_leakage()=FAIL (exact hash cited) -> same directory, fix applied ->
audit_leakage()=PASS, tile correctly excluded, manifest count drops by
exactly one. Live CLI smoke test of real run_ksweep.main() (K=3/4, real
subprocess training, real checkpoints) confirmed the leak tile dropped
before K-subset formation. The leakage checker itself was never touched
or weakened.

Data-side finding: the exact historical union_tiles directory that
produced the original 2026-09-19 FAIL no longer exists -- the current
real 562-tile set already passes audit_leakage() as-is. Nothing to
physically rebuild.

Full retrain assessed as BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: ~7.2 hours estimated on this
machine's CPU-only Torch (no CUDA) for one full production K-sweep.
No currently-trusted checkpoint is invalidated by this -- none existed
with verified cryptographic provenance either before or after this fix.

head_commit.message:
fix(domain_gap): add structural mtime-authority guard to run_alignment_and_matching.py

GAP-012: _safe_latest_output_dir and _find_latest_final_xodr sorted
candidates by mtime alone (os.path.getmtime / Path.stat().st_mtime) with
no structural/content guard before treating the newest-by-mtime
file/directory as authoritative -- the repo's known false-green
mtime-authority anti-pattern (a stale file touched by an unrelated
process, a clock skew, or a restored backup could win purely on mtime).

Fix follows the established, tested convention from
ultimate_pipeline/tools/artifact_locator.py::_newest_final_xodr:

- _find_latest_final_xodr now reuses artifact_locator's
  _repaired_sibling_exists() to prefer XODR candidates that are
  structurally verified post-repair (a same-run *_laneSectionFixed*.xodr
  sibling exists on disk) before ever consulting mtime; mtime is only
  the tie-breaker among structurally-equal candidates (or the full
  fallback when no candidate carries repair evidence).

- _safe_latest_output_dir gains a new _run_dir_has_completed_output()
  guard: prefer run directories that contain a written 08_final*.xodr
  (real completed-run evidence) over raw mtime ordering; mtime is only
  the tie-breaker among directories that are equally legitimate by that
  structural check.

Also adds ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_mtime_audit.py, the
regression guard cited by GAP-012 (present upstream on
fix/xodr-validator-convergence-v1-20260921 but missing from this
branch's base, integration/production-large-map-20260918) so the guard
is enforced going forward. All 14 PROTECTED_PACKAGES modules pass,
including run_alignment_and_matching.py.

Verified: full bare `pytest` run -- 5904 passed, 5 skipped, 4 failed
(all 4 pre-existing failures in tests/unit/test_regen_find_final_xodr_hygiene.py,
unrelated to this change -- confirmed identical failures with this
commit's diff stashed out; that file exercises
scripts/regen_map_of_record.py / ultimate_pipeline/contracts/artifact_authority.py,
neither touched here).
